summary: The household's frozen history test rejected all six pre-registered stock rules: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally did better than the core and than any rule. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. Four watch notes, all neutral and low; nothing is expected to beat the index, and real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain looked at old races and saw that its ways of picking runners did no better than picking names out of a hat. So today it only watches four runners and bets nothing real. The stock calls are pretend money; the family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. This week we do what we do every week: the long-term money buys the whole-market fund, the money we may need soon stays safe, and nothing gets rushed because the market had a grey day. A sideways market is weather, not news.

Second, the pretend game. Our history test is in and it is humbling: every stock rule we wrote down did no better than names drawn from a hat, and simply owning every name on the list equally beat them all. The paper book is a little ahead of the core after a couple of weeks, which tells us almost nothing. The weekly bet game has no scored weeks yet, and last week's open bet is trailing. Luck alone wins about half the weeks, so a few weeks prove nothing either way.

Third, the lesson. Picking felt like it should help, and on this list it took value away. A gardener who keeps pulling up plants to check the roots grows less than one who waters and waits.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a tested rule that beats random picks on history, then half a year of paper record ahead of the core, with names passing our checks beating the benchmark by a clear margin. Until then, we watch and learn.

With care, the brain

bets.why: Same ranking as last week: steady names passing most checks and moving little with the market on top, fallen names failing most checks and swinging with it at the bottom. The checks have shown no edge, so this is a test, not a belief.

But its swings are much larger than the benchmark's, it already sits inside the band the library calls extended above its long average, and the history test rejected every rule built on such checks. The checklist is mixed with fading volume and too thin a reward-to-risk for a new paper entry. Same neutral, low call as recent runs; the data did not change.
